questions.q: When should you build a custom spoke action rather than reach for an official spoke?
options: Every time, even when an official spoke already covers the system
When no official spoke exists for the external system the business needs to integrate with
Only when the MID Server is unavailable
Never — custom actions are not a real IntegrationHub capability
questions.explain: Custom actions fill the gap left by systems, like a niche internal platform, with no official ServiceNow-maintained spoke.

questions.q: What are the three parts of a custom action, in order?
options: A screenshot, a script, and a report
Outputs only, with no Inputs or internal logic
Inputs, an internal step sequence (typically a REST step), and Outputs
A Spoke license, a REST Message, and a MID Server
questions.explain: Every custom action defines named Inputs, an internal sequence of steps (usually a single REST step), and named Outputs mapped from the response.

questions.q: How does the REST step inside a custom action differ from course 4's generic REST step dropped directly on a flow's canvas?
options: It cannot call any external API at all
It requires a MID Server in every case
It is identical in every respect, with no practical difference
It's configured once inside the action and then reused by every flow that calls the action, rather than configured per flow
questions.explain: The internal REST step is defined once inside the action; the action itself, not the raw REST step, becomes the reusable unit across flows.

questions.q: What does a flow builder who consumes someone else's custom action actually see?
options: Named Inputs and Outputs, the same as they'd see using any official spoke's action
The internal REST step's endpoint URL, which they must configure themselves
The Authentication Profile's credentials in plain text
The target system's raw API documentation
questions.explain: Consumers interact with Inputs and Outputs only — the custom action hides the underlying REST call and authentication, just like an official spoke.

questions.q: What should you check before publishing a custom action for other flow builders to use?
options: That Inputs/Outputs are clearly named and useful, and the Authentication Profile is meant for shared, ongoing use rather than a personal token
That the action exposes every raw field the API returns, regardless of need
That no Authentication Profile is attached at all
Nothing — custom actions require no review before publishing
questions.explain: A published custom action becomes something other teams depend on, so clear naming, a minimal Output surface, and durable shared authentication all matter before release.
